physicalDetails.detail: Eight or nine years old. Hair matted flat against her head; face smeared, mouth 'too dark at the corners' with a ring of dirt from licking cellar wall and biting turnips. Thin arms. One stocking on, the other foot bare and black to the ankle; the stocking has a darn at the heel in a different wool (brown in grey), 'close and neat'. Clutches a scrap of blue cloth ('blanket', 'the blue scrap') in her right fist, knuckles white, throughout the chapter.
Dehydrated, hoarse, weeping without enough breath to do it properly; too weak at first to draw the bolt. Wears somebody's cut-down cloak at the departure.

voiceMarkers.detail: A cracked whisper that gains a little wet strength with water. Direct, matter-of-fact, child's idiom: 'Say it again.', 'You talk funny.', 'Da said not to open it. Not for anybody. Not if it was him.', 'Mam died.', 'Her breath went sweet... Pears gone brown.', 'We didn't have any pears.', 'Missus Hale's baby. Then Mister Pell.', 'Da held the glass to her mouth. His shaving glass. It didn't go misty.', 'Hundreds. All night. Every night.', 'It was always dark.', 'Up the north road.', 'Past Pell's. Up the cow way.' Speaks to Neral's shoulder and not to the others.

beliefs.belief: Her father said not to open the hatch for anybody, 'not if it was him' (the 'him' is not clarified on page; it reads as the father speaking of himself); she kept it bolted until a voice that talked funny said it had water.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Ambiguous on page: 'Not if it was him' reads as the father speaking of himself; his fate is unknown.

beliefs.belief: The north road is the way the dead walked ('Up the north road'), which she defines as the way past Pell's and up the cow way (a child's name for the road at the top of her lane).
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Reconciled on the ground by the drove way at first light: the dead went up the cow way north and a little east, not the Pass road.

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Hold on to Neral and the blue scrap on the ride north.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Shocked, wary, rigid; trusts Neral only; sits 'bolt upright' with her hands in the bay's mane.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Drew the bolt from below after Neral's water trickled through the crack, though her hands were too weak and it took two tries.
Came out of the turnip heap on hands and knees for the water; gave a testimony of fragments to Neral, not to the others.
Took one step and another toward the bay and put her cheek against Neral's saddle skirt; let Neral lift her on.

abilitiesDemonstrated.ability: Survived days in a sealed cellar on raw turnips and the wet off the wall; kept the hatch bolted while the dead walked past; located direction by looking through a barred cellar slot at the lane at dog-nose height.

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Neral
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: No name (asked once, the girl shook her head; Neral let it go). 'you' and quiet phrases.

howOthersAddressHer.speaker: Sylvanas
howOthersAddressHer.pattern: No address except 'Which is the north road?'; thinks of her as 'the child', 'the girl'.

howSheAddressesOthers.pattern: No name used; speaks into her shoulder.

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Ducks behind the turnip heap; hides her face in Neral's collar and shoulder from everyone else; goes white round the mouth at the bay; flinches at Sylvanas's flat voice; her head goes loose on Neral's shoulder in sleep 'all at once'; watches Sylvanas 'the way a hare watches a hawk go over, without moving anything but her eyes'; fist clenched and unclenched on the blue scrap; stiff 'as a doll' when lifted on the saddle.

knowledge.detail: Order of the sickness in Millhaven: Missus Hale's baby, then Mister Pell, then everybody coughing at the well; Mam told her not to stand near them.
Her mother's breath went sweet like pears gone brown before she was hot; her mother said she'd been at the pears, but they had none.
In the last days callers at the house: Gran Ottley (to sit with Mam), the newer grain seller (cheaper than Mister Hollis; Da and Mam had words about him), the tinker (for the pot).
Mam died; Da held his shaving glass to her mouth and it did not mist; 'then she got up, in the dark'; Da put the girl down the cellar and told her to bolt it.
Heard feet dragging past the cellar slot, up the back toward Pell's, 'hundreds, all night, every night'; cannot say how many nights; does not know where her father is.

arc.currentPosition: Sent north with Neral; never continues south (plan). Fate at the Pass is off the southbound page.
